acceptance.description: Acceptance-test scaffolding. Off everywhere except a bench cluster running the snowplow live-refresh acceptance harness. Separate from observability.snowplowSli because they answer different questions: that one is a dashboard an operator may want, this is test scaffolding nobody else should carry.
acceptance.title: acceptance

s6Probe.description: Add a route-only (label-less) /s6-probe nav entry whose content resolves by the page:<slug> convention to flexes/page-s6-probe — a page CR the harness creates and deletes per run. Needed because a page root alone does not serve a route, and the SPA only arms a widget it actually renders: without it the harness can create a widget, delete it, observe nothing and report a clean pass, having proved only that it never armed. Nothing renders in the sidebar; with no harness the route resolves to a page that does not exist.
s6Probe.title: s6Probe

agents.description: The agent control plane ships as the separate portal-agents chart.

enabled.description: Show the Agents sidebar entry and its /agents routes. Set true ONLY when portal-agents is installed: a nav ref whose target is missing stays visible and 404s.

enableAdminUser.description: Enable admin user (basic authentication) with cluster-admin permissions
enableAdminUser.title: enableAdminUser

enableCyberjokerUser.description: Enable cyberjoker user (basic authentication) with namespace-scoped permissions
enableCyberjokerUser.title: enableCyberjokerUser

enableDemoSystemNamespace.description: enabling the demo creates the demo-system namespace, deploys two Route resources within it, and grants permissions to the cyberjoker user if that user is enabled
enableDemoSystemNamespace.title: enableDemoSystemNamespace

marketplace.description: Where the portal reads the blueprint/operator marketplace catalog. configmap (default) = the in-cluster ConfigMap the krateo-marketplace-catalog composition renders; external = the legacy blueprints-endpoint Helm-repo (one-release fallback).

observabilityConsoleUrl.description: Optional URL of the external observability console (e.g. the clickstack/HyperDX UI). When set, a "View in console" link appears on the /observability page and opens it in a new tab; empty hides the link. No default target is invented — a deployer must point this at their own console.
observabilityConsoleUrl.title: observabilityConsoleUrl

spokeReadbackCluster.description: W3-3 spoke read-back binding — the ONE registered spoke cluster whose /clusters/{name} detail page shows LIVE compositions read directly from the spoke apiserver (restaction cluster-compositions). snowplow endpointRef references are static (not jq-templated), so the read-back is bound per-install; generating a per-spoke RESTAction + endpoint Secret pair at registration time is the follow-up that removes this value.
spokeReadbackCluster.title: spokeReadbackCluster

spokeReadbackEndpointNamespace.description: Namespace of the derived spoke endpoint Secret (must be readable by snowplow's ServiceAccount; the authn namespace krateo-system is the canonical home, same place the registration flow keeps the kubeconfig Secret).
spokeReadbackEndpointNamespace.title: spokeReadbackEndpointNamespace

spokeReadbackEndpointSecret.description: Name of the DERIVED endpoint Secret for the spoke read-back — snowplow endpoint shape {server-url, token, insecure, certificate-authority-data}, derived from the registered spoke's kubeconfig Secret (NOT the kubeconfig Secret itself, which snowplow cannot consume). The server-url deliberately carries the /apis suffix; see restaction.cluster-compositions.yaml for why.
spokeReadbackEndpointSecret.title: spokeReadbackEndpointSecret

tenant.description: Display name of the platform tenant — shown in the sider tenant chip and the page eyebrows (dashboard greeting, compositions, observability). A deployer-set label, not derived data; defaults to krateo-enterprise.
tenant.title: tenant

tiers.description: RBAC namespace tiers for portal page widgets. Each page-root Flex is placed in one tier; the sidebar Menu references it there, so snowplow resolves visibility AS THE USER and the frontend hides pages the user's Role cannot GET. Empty string = .Release.Namespace (the default single-namespace layout, no RBAC tiering). Set `admin` (and optionally `tenant`) to distinct namespaces to split page visibility by audience.
tiers.title: tiers

common.description: Shared chrome + pages every authenticated user sees (Dashboard). Empty = release namespace.
common.title: common

tenant.description: Pages a tenant persona sees (Blueprints). Empty = release namespace (collapsed onto common).
tenant.title: tenant

admin.description: Admin-only pages (Compositions, Clusters, Observability, Incidents, Alerts, Marketplace, Settings, the three Builders). Empty = release namespace.
admin.title: admin

previewSandbox.description: Where the Autopilot live preview applies its draft widget CRs. MUST match the frontend chart's previewSandbox, which OWNS the namespace, its quota and its RBAC — this chart only reads it, to list in-flight drafts on the Portal Builder page so a person can resume one.

namespace.description: Namespace holding preview drafts. Read-only from this chart.

alerts.description: SRE/MSP alert catalogue — the Kubernetes checks an operator is expected to have (crash loops, OOM kills, unschedulable pods, node pressure, failing probes, stuck volumes, dead telemetry), shipped as Alert CRs so a fresh install is not silent. Requires the observability component, which owns the Alert CRD. Saturation checks (CPU/memory/disk/PV percentages, certificate days remaining) are deliberately absent: the Alert CRD counts rows in a logs source and cannot address a metric, so they are blocked on alert-troubleshooter#34.

enabled.description: Ship the catalogue. Off by default: it needs the Alert CRD, and every firing alert starts a model-driven RCA and opens a TroubleshootingReport (one per alert), so it carries a running cost a deployer should choose rather than inherit.

extended.description: Also ship the extended tier: catch-all and baseline-relative alerts whose thresholds mean 'far above normal' rather than 'anything at all', and which need retuning per cluster. The core tier is the set that should stay quiet when nothing is wrong.

disabled.description: Catalogue entries to skip, by name — lets a deployer drop an alert that does not apply (no LoadBalancers, no preemptible nodes, no persistent volumes) without forking the chart.

thresholds.description: Per-alert threshold overrides keyed by catalogue name. The shipped defaults come from a real cluster's measured baseline and are a starting point, not a claim about yours.
